title: Question units (A2 output)
description: One self-contained unit per visual/worksheet, plus the container envelope that makes C3 able to write a real question.

vendor.description: The run's BI vendor (the name of an installed BI reader (`metrics_agent.readers`). Any string here: which readers exist is checked against the installed ones at S0, never fixed in this schema.); `mixed` when its BI models come from different vendors (see `vendors`).

home_table.description: A `formula_language: sql` measure's home table, by the model's own (logical) name: the role its formula is placed over.

addressing.description: The view's columns the calculation runs ALONG, in order (outer first): the window's ORDER BY. Each sorts ascending with an empty value first, as the BI tool lays the view out.

partitioning.description: The view's columns the calculation restarts on: the window's PARTITION BY. Every grouped column is in exactly one of the two lists.

pad.description: A crosstab the view densifies for this calculation: the columns on its rows and on its columns. Every row tuple is laid out against every column tuple, the empty cells included, before the calculation runs (checked live).

sort.description: The view's own order of an addressed column, where it is not ascending: the window runs along the columns in the order the view shows them (checked live: a computed, a manual and a descending sort).

members.description: A manual order: the members first to last (null: the empty member).

by.description: The aggregate a computed sort orders the members by, in the formula language.

within.description: A nested sort: the columns of its shelf outside it, within each of whose members it orders.

nested.description: The compute-using of each table calculation the measure reaches through another calc, by that calc's name: its own columns to run along and restart on (checked live: Tableau runs a nested calc by its own compute-using, Table (across) when the file names none; a secondary calculation nests the one it runs over).

refusal.description: Why the calculation has no statement: the measure is refused with this reason, never compiled without its post-aggregation step.

table_calc.description: A measure computed over the statement's aggregated rows (A1 usage `table_calcs`), with its columns named as the unit's `group_by` names them.

visual_calc.description: true: the measure is one of the view's own calculations (`visual_matrix.calcs`), its formula that calculation's expression.

hidden.description: true: the view computes the measure for its own calculations but does not show it; the statements leave it out.

group_by_tables.description: OPTIONAL, parallel to `group_by`: the warehouse table each grouping column is read from, or null where the BI file does not say (then a column on the statement's own table is read there, else on the one unit table that has it).

negated.description: true when an enclosing NOT excludes this predicate rather than requiring it

value_kind.description: what the predicate compares the column to; only a literal can be tuned

table.description: The warehouse table the filter column is read from, when the BI file says which model table it belongs to; absent or null: read off the statement's own table first.

null_as.description: The value an EMPTY cell takes in this filter's comparisons, by the type of the value it is compared with (the tool's own comparison rule): a number, the text, a date. A comparison the stand-in passes keeps the rows with no value too (`qty < 5` keeps the empty quantities when an empty number is 0). Absent: an empty cell passes no comparison (SQL's rule). Not used by a membership (`in`), a null test, a text match or a relative range.

measure.description: Set on a `measure`-stage filter that tests a MEASURE (the model's, or a column aggregated at the use site) at the view's grain: the measure's name. The condition (`op`, `value`) applies to the measure's value on each row of the view, after aggregation; on a view with no grouping, to its one total.

cardinality.description: FROM-end:TO-end multiplicity in the `<M|1>:<M|1>` vocabulary ('M:1', '1:1', 'M:M', '1:M'), or 'unknown'. A join never walks from the one end to the many end, and a TO end whose multiplicity is not one (M:M, unknown) is read as its distinct rows, so it never multiplies the FROM rows.

cross_filter.description: Which way a filter crosses the relationship: 'single' (the TO end filters the FROM end only) or 'both' (either end filters the other). Absent or null: 'single'.

is_active.description: false for a relationship the model declares but does not use unless a measure activates it: a statement never joins along it. Absent: true.

name.description: The relationship's own name in the model.

from_role.description: The model's name for the FROM end (a table's `logical_name`). A table the model uses under two names is two roles, and each keeps its own.

to_role.description: The model's name for the TO end.

columns.description: EVERY key column pair of the relationship, in order. `from_column` and `to_column` are the first pair, kept for readers of the one-pair shape; a join is written on all of them.

condition.description: A range or as-of relationship's condition, verbatim.

join_type.description: Which unmatched rows a statement that joins along this relationship keeps: a row of one end whose key matches no row of the other end (an orphan or a NULL key). 'left': a row of the MANY end (of the FROM end, when neither or both ends are many) is kept, under a NULL member of every column of the other end (the BI tool's blank member), and an unmatched row of the other end is not. 'full': an unmatched row of EITHER end is kept (a relationship that aggregates each table at its own grain and keeps what does not match). 'inner': neither is kept (a relationship the tool treats as limited, or one that assumes referential integrity). Absent or null: 'left'. The reader decides it from the model's own settings; the compiler only applies it.

rely_on_referential_integrity.description: The model states that every FROM-end key has a TO-end match (assume referential integrity), so the tool joins it as an inner join. Carried as read; `join_type` already says what it means for a join.

siblings_omitted.description: How many more widgets the dashboard holds than `siblings` lists: present only when the bi.max_sibling_widgets cap cut the list, which keeps the nearest.

negated.description: true when an enclosing NOT excludes this predicate rather than requiring it

value_kind.description: what the predicate compares the column to; only a literal can be tuned

table.description: The table the filter column is on, when the BI file says so (see the unit's `filters`).

null_as.description: The value an EMPTY cell takes in this filter's comparisons, by the type of the value it is compared with (the tool's own comparison rule): a number, the text, a date. A comparison the stand-in passes keeps the rows with no value too (`qty < 5` keeps the empty quantities when an empty number is 0). Absent: an empty cell passes no comparison (SQL's rule). Not used by a membership (`in`), a null test, a text match or a relative range.

measure.description: Set on a `measure`-stage filter that tests a MEASURE (the model's, or a column aggregated at the use site) at the view's grain: the measure's name. The condition (`op`, `value`) applies to the measure's value on each row of the view, after aggregation; on a view with no grouping, to its one total.

assets.description: The BI assets behind this unit — model-level ones and the unit's own — with the tool's own ids and, where a BI plug resolved them (`bi_assets`), their catalogue ids and qualified names.

domain.description: Deterministic: the BI workbook/report name, verbatim. No clustering.

bi_context.description: The bounded, named metadata block C3 reads INSTEAD of loading the BI files. It carries the human-authored layer A1's facts contract discards — which is most of the business context — at a few hundred bytes per unit rather than two file reads. It is also reviewable and testable, which a file the model may or may not have opened is not.

measures.description: Each measure the widget shows, as the model defines it (lib/bi_tags.py): name, caption, aggregation, folder, format string, and the model's own context about it, each text cut at policy `bi.max_context_chars`. CONTEXT, NEVER SEMANTICS: no compiler reads it.

style.description: `explicit`, `implicit` (aggregated where it is used), `report` (a report's own measure), `kpi_target`, `kpi_status`.

tags.description: annotations, perspectives, the model's endorsement (and its note), a KPI's target and status.

siblings_omitted.description: How many more widgets the dashboard holds than `siblings` lists: present only when the bi.max_sibling_widgets cap cut the list, which keeps the nearest.

dimensions.description: Columns the BI model itself declares as dimensions (role=dimension). A filter-shelf-only field appears here and nowhere else.

native_source.description: Set when every measure in the unit lives on ONE table whose source is a statement (`source_lineage.native_sql`): a native query, or a custom-SQL datasource. The compiler then reads the query's result set as a derived table, and `columns` maps each model column (by name) to the query's own output column.

expression_language.description: The formula language the widget's calculated fields are written in, set by the reader when a column, a filter or the sort it names may be a calculated field: such a field is an EXPRESSION, compiled from its formula like a measure, never read as a stored column. Absent when the source's widgets name only stored columns. The compiler decides from this, never from which tool wrote the unit. Carried from the BI usage entry.

blank_rows.description: OPTIONAL. What the view does with a row whose every measure is empty. `hidden`: the view leaves it out; the compiler keeps the rows where at least one value is not NULL (a HAVING over the statement's own value expressions, which a reader of the statement treats as hiding empty rows, not as a restriction). `shown`: the view also lists the members with no rows at all ("show items with no data"): every member of the grouping columns (the combinations one table holds, crossed between tables) joined to the rows' values. Absent: the view shows the rows the statement returns.

kind.description: `grand_total`: keeps no grouping column. `subtotal`: keeps some of them.

group_by.description: The grouping columns the total row keeps, named as the unit's group_by names them (a subset of it, in its order).

totals.description: OPTIONAL. The total rows the view shows beside its leaf rows (a table's grand total, a matrix's row and column subtotals and grand totals), one entry per total grain. A total is the measures evaluated over the total's own context (the view's filters, grouped by only the columns the total keeps), never a sum of the leaf rows: a distinct count, a ratio or an average total differs from the sum. Each grain is its own statement (`candidates.totals`); the leaf statement keeps its plain shape. Absent or empty: the view shows no total rows.

distinct_rows.description: OPTIONAL. true: the view has no measure and lists the distinct combinations of its columns that exist (a table of columns only). Over one table: that table's distinct rows. Over several: the combinations that exist in the table every one of them is reached from along many-to-one relationships. The unit is a grouping with no aggregate, never dropped as decoration.

visual_matrix.description: OPTIONAL. The view's own calculations over its matrix (Power BI calls them visual calculations): each is evaluated on every cell of the matrix the view lays out (its leaf rows and every total level of each axis, the empty cells of a two-axis matrix included), in the order of the axes' columns, and may read other cells (a running sum, the previous row, the parent total, a lookup). Written only where the view has one. The leaf statement and each total statement read the matrix at their own level. Axis columns are named as `group_by` is; measures as `measures`, where a calculation shown is a measure with `visual_calc: true` and a measure the view hides has `hidden: true`.

language.description: The language the calculations are written in.

rows.description: The axis' levels, outer first; each level lists the grouping columns it holds (a table visual holds all its columns in one level).

columns.description: The axis' levels, outer first; each level lists the grouping columns it holds (a table visual holds all its columns in one level).

pages.description: The axis' levels, outer first; each level lists the grouping columns it holds (a table visual holds all its columns in one level).

expression.description: As the file saves it; its references are names in `refs`.

hidden.description: true: in the matrix (other calculations read it) but not shown.

refs.description: Each name an expression references -> what it is: a grouping column, a measure of the view (by its name in `measures`), or another calculation.

hidden.description: The view's measures that are in the matrix but not shown (the calculations read them).

max_values_grouped.description: OPTIONAL. The view groups by a column of a table of fixed rows no relationship reaches (a parameter), which compiles one statement per value it shows: the most values the statement holds (policy bi.max_variants_per_widget). A value over it is left out and named (`variant_cap`); the unit is then partial.

parameters.description: OPTIONAL. The values the view takes when it is OPENED (a page another page navigates to with the member a person picked): each a member of `column` (of `table`), which narrows the view to that member. The view saved with no value shows its whole population; a variant unit (`variant_of`) answers it for every member at once, grouped by the column.

kind.description: `member`: one member of `column`, chosen by the person who opens the view.

keeps_filters.description: Whether the filters of the view it is opened from apply too (unknown until then; recorded, not compiled).

variant_of.description: OPTIONAL. The unit this one is a variant of: the same widget answered another way it can show (another field a viewer can switch it to, the value it takes for each member it can be opened with, the latest point of its trend). `variant` says which.

variant.description: OPTIONAL. Which variant of `variant_of` this unit is, in words.

vendors.description: Present when the run reads several BI models: each distinct vendor, sorted. `vendor` is their shared vendor, or `mixed` when they differ.

vendor_id.description: The BI tool's own id for the asset. Null when the input does not state one; never invented.

site.description: The BI tool's site or workspace the asset lives in.

catalog_id.description: The asset's id in the catalogue a BI plug resolved it in (its `bi_assets`), joined at A2 by role and name; null without one.

endorsement.description: The BI tool's endorsement of the asset (bi_facts asset `endorsement`).

labels.description: The BI tool's own tags on the asset (content tags), verbatim.

declared.description: The declared metric this unit compiles (bi_facts `measures[].declared`), with the model that declares it. Carried on the statement (provenance.bi.declared) to X1-X3, which hold a card built from it to it. A declared metric is identified by `model` and `metric` together.

description.description: The model's comment on the metric, verbatim.

synonyms.description: The model's own other names for this, verbatim. Retrieval words, never interpreted.

entity.description: The physical table the metric is computed over.

formula.description: The formula with every fact, dimension and metric it names expanded to what it stands for.

grain.description: The entity's declared key, fully qualified.

source.description: The FROM clause: the entity, then a LEFT JOIN for every join in `joins`, on every key column.

joins.description: Every join the formula and the dimensions need. Never one that fans out: many-to-one, or one-to-one.

dimensions.description: Every dimension the model declares on a table the metric reaches. A levelled time expression (a date part over one column) is not one; the bare date is.

datatype.description: The type the model declares; else `date` or `boolean` when the model's own SQL treats the column so (only the DATE argument of a date function counts); else `unknown`. A number is never a date.

description.description: The model's comment on the dimension, verbatim.

synonyms.description: The model's own other names for this, verbatim. Retrieval words, never interpreted.

examples.description: The model's example questions that read this metric, each with its SQL over the base tables.

group_by.description: The declared dimensions (by `name` above) the example groups by.

timeframe_column.description: The date the metric's examples restrict or group by, when they name exactly one.
